newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish government seals shipyard holding group.
newsitem.headline: Polish government seals shipyard holding group.

text.p: The Polish government Tuesday pushed ahead with the creation of a shipbuilding group to help the industry survive foreign competition, Finance Minister Marek Belka said.

Belka said the government, tired of waiting for results of talks among the group's would-be members, decided to kick-start the plan by giving its 46 percent stake in the ailing Gdynia shipyard to the sucessful Szczecin yard.
Under the plan Stocznia Szczecin SA would also take control of a majority stake in troubled ship-engine maker H. Cegielski and possibly other firms, he said.
The Szczecin shipyard will subsequently buy Gdynia's new stock issue, which may double its capital, said Szczecin's President Krzysztof Piotrowski.
Poland's state-owned Bank Handlowy will also hand over its 18 percent stake in Gdynia to Szczecin, Belka said.
Following the launch of free market reforms seven years ago, Szczecin was the only shipyard to undergo successful restructuring, enabling it to compete with the world's best companies.

In the Szczecin shipyard, employees now have 34.7 percent of shares, a group of four Polish banks has 30 percent, with 15 percent in the hands of Capital Group Ltd, 9 percent owned by the management and 5.3 percent by small shareholders.
The treasury now has 46 percent of Gdynia. Among its other shareholders are the state-owned commercial Pomorski Bank Kredytowy SA which has 20.5 percent of shares and Bank Handlowy with 18.7 percent.
